candidate.answerReason: Josh's distance was 2 times 4/5, or 8/5, of Mike's distance. Their distances split the 13 miles in the ratio 8:5, so Mike rode 5 miles.

methods.label: Combine the time and rate ratios
methods.explanation:
Distance equals rate times riding time, so both comparisons affect how far Josh rode. He rode for twice as long as Mike at \(\frac45\) of Mike's rate. His distance was therefore
\[
2\cdot\frac45=\frac85
\]
times Mike's distance. Thus Josh's and Mike's distances were in the ratio \(8:5\).

Because they rode toward each other and met, their distances add to \(13\) miles. The ratio has \(8+5=13\) equal parts, so each part represents \(13/13=1\) mile. Mike rode five parts, or \(\boxed{5\text{ miles}}\), choice B.
